subject: Post-call: Redwood integration & SDK fit / next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Duran <alex.duran@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Redwood integration & SDK fit / next steps

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the call today — great to meet you and Samir. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned. Please flag anything I missed.

TL;DR
- Primary pain: slow, expensive search & reranking across clinical notes and triage responses; current vector infra adds latency and costs.
- Goal: 1) improve semantic search relevance + reranking, 2) stream long model responses into the UI without blocking, 3) support structured outputs for downstream EHR ingestion.
- Redwood fit: embeddings + reranker for recall -> rerank; streaming & chunked generation for long responses; function calling/structured output to produce JSON events for ingestion.

Key points from the call
- Data & volume: ~50M notes, peak query rate ~350 qps, average sequence length 1k tokens for context windows.
- Current infra: self-hosted vector db with batching at app layer; misses token-level caching and KV reuse.
- Risk: need predictable latency for triage flows and HIPAA-compliant hosting.

Integration / product fit notes (technical)
- Embeddings & reranking: we recommend the 1536-d embedding model for initial pilot. Typical flow: store embeddings in your vector DB, query top-K, then call Redwood reranking endpoint to score/merge. This reduces endpoint load and gives stronger final ranking.
- Streaming: use Redwood's streaming SDK (Python/TS) to push tokens as they arrive — avoids client-side blocking for long outputs. We discussed chunked context upload and early exits when confidence thresholds met.
- Function calling & structured outputs: use the function-calling surface to return validated JSON shapes (e.g., {"finding":..., "confidence":...}) so your ingestion pipeline can consume without additional parsing. We also support schema validation and strict-mode outputs.
- SDK changes: minimal — you can use the existing Python/TS SDKs. We'll provide a sample call that shows: init client -> stream -> on_token callback -> final structured JSON via function call. Dev will help with code samples.
- Model selection & cost: suggest starting on the rwd-medium variant with quantized weights for cost-efficient throughput in Dedicated. We'll provide bench numbers for your sequence length distribution.
- Security & hosting: Redwood Private (VPC) + KMS for keys; SOC 2 evidence and OKTA SSO support are available.

Attachments: integration_diagram.png (high level flow), redwood_pricing.pdf (pilot pricing + Dedicated sizing).

Proposed next steps
1) Schedule technical deep-dive with Dev Patel (solutions engineer) to walk the sample code and perf numbers — target 60 min next week.
2) Share a short mutual action plan (I’ll draft) with milestones: pilot env, latency SLO, success criteria, trial tokens.
3) Provide access to a sandbox account (read-only telemetry) and a small Dedicated trial for load testing (subject to PO).

Can you share Samir’s availability next week? I’ll send a calendar invite once we lock a slot.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0128

On attachments: integration_diagram.png (see callout on streaming / KV cache), redwood_pricing.pdf (includes pilot estimate + 3-month dedicated sizing)
From: Alex Duran <alex.duran@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Khan <samir.khan@acmehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 16:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Redwood integration & SDK fit / next steps

Marissa —

Thanks for the thorough recap, this matches our notes. A few clarifying Qs before we schedule the technical deep-dive:

1) Embedding dimensionality: you recommended 1536 — what’s the impact on index size and recall vs. the smaller 768 option? We need to estimate storage + refresh costs.
2) Reranker throughput: does the reranker operate as a separate inference call per candidate or can it batch-score a list efficiently? Our current function does per-candidate scoring which is the bottleneck.
3) Trial logistics: what does the Dedicated trial include? Are there any limits on model variants during the trial?

Samir and I can do Tuesday (Sep 1) or Thursday (Sep 3) mornings PST.

—Alex
Product Lead, Search & Insights
Acme Health
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Duran <alex.duran@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 17:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Redwood integration & SDK fit / next steps

Thanks Alex — great questions, answered inline and with next actions.

1) Embedding dimensionality: the 1536-d vectors improve recall on clinical queries by ~3-5% in our benchmarks vs 768 for domain-specific corpora; storage grows ~2x. For your 50M notes that implies ~6–8 TB raw for 1536 (depending on compression). We’ll include a cost/benefit table in the MAP draft.

2) Reranker throughput: Redwood supports batched reranking — you can send a candidate list (up to 64 candidates per request) and we’ll score them in a single call. This is much more efficient than per-candidate calls and reduces latency/cost significantly; Dev will demo batching patterns and the best K to request.

3) Dedicated trial: includes a 2-week Dedicated pool sized for a pilot (we’ll propose GPU topology based on the perf numbers we share). Trial allows most model variants but large experimental quantized-only variants may be restricted; we’ll propose the rwd-medium / quantized baseline for cost tests.

Next actions — I’ll take these items:
- Draft the mutual action plan and cost breakdown by Tue EOD (I’ll attach it into HubSpot record).
- Dev to send a 30–45 min technical deep-dive invite (recommended attendees: Samir, Alex, 1 infra engineer).
- Provision sandbox tokens and a read-only telemetry export (ETA 3 business days after NDA).

Dev / Rishi — can you confirm Dev’s availability Tue Sep 1 10:00–11:00 PST or Thu Sep 3 09:00–10:00 PST? I’ll send the calendar invite once we confirm.

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Best,
Marissa
